s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive swelling of the manubrium with a history of previous thyroid surgery
salient_findings: Lytic lesion replacing the manubrium on CT imaging
Follicular thyroid cells on fine-needle aspiration
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
Previous resection of a large left substernal thyroid lobe 12 years ago
Swelling of the manubrium is slightly tender
Swelling increased in size over the month prior to presentation
CT imaging shows a lytic lesion replacing the manubrium
Lytic lesion is in close proximity to the brachiocephalic artery and the left innominate vein
Fine-needle aspiration revealed follicular thyroid cells
Pathological examination shows thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae

shortlist.label: Ectopic thyroid carcinoma in the manubrium
shortlist.why_kept: History of previous thyroid surgery and presence of thyroid follicles in the manubrial lesion

shortlist.label: Follicular thyroid carcinoma with distant metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic lesion replacing the manubrium and presence of follicular thyroid cells in the fine-needle aspiration

shortlist.label: Hurthle cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation and histological features to follicular thyroid carcinoma

shortlist.label: Thyroid metastasis to the sternum
shortlist.why_kept: History of previous thyroid surgery and presence of a lytic lesion in the manubrium

raw.rationale: The presence of a lytic lesion in the manubrium with follicular thyroid cells on fine-needle aspiration and pathological examination showing thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae, suggests malignant transformation and metastasis, particularly given the patient's history of previous thyroid surgery.

rejected.label: Recurrent benign goiter
rejected.why: The aggressive nature of the lytic lesion and its rapid growth, along with the infiltration of thyroid follicles into bone trabeculae, are not typical of benign goiter.
